------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.
  -- Step 2: Keep only the partial order part; totality is dropped.
  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.
  ×-pw-isEquivalence t₁ t₂ = (Pointwise.×-isEquivalence (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ t₂))

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.
  -- Step 2: The antisymmetry axiom states that for all elements x and y of A, if x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ x, then x ≈₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a and c be elements of A with a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a. Instantiate the antisymmetry axiom with x = a and y = c. The two premises required are exactly a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a, which we have by assumption.
  -- Step 4: The antisymmetry axiom therefore yields a ≈₁ c, which is the required conclusion.
  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_. Its partial order component is a preorder, so the relation ≤₁ is transitive: whenever x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ z, we have x ≤₁ z.
  -- Step 2: The same preorder structure gives reflexivity of the order up to equality: whenever x ≈₁ y, we have x ≤₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.
  -- Step 2: Keep only the partial order part; totality is dropped.
  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.
  ×-pw-isEquivalence t₁ t₂ = (Pointwise.×-isEquivalence (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ t₂))

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.
  -- Step 2: The antisymmetry axiom states that for all elements x and y of A, if x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ x, then x ≈₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a and c be elements of A with a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a. Instantiate the antisymmetry axiom with x = a and y = c. The two premises required are exactly a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a, which we have by assumption.
  -- Step 4: The antisymmetry axiom therefore yields a ≈₁ c, which is the required conclusion.
  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_. Its partial order component is a preorder, so the relation ≤₁ is transitive: whenever x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ z, we have x ≤₁ z.
  -- Step 2: The same preorder structure gives reflexivity of the order up to equality: whenever x ≈₁ y, we have x ≤₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.
  -- Step 2: Keep only the partial order part; totality is dropped.
  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.
  ×-pw-isEquivalence t₁ t₂ = (Pointwise.×-isEquivalence (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ t₂))

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.
  -- Step 2: The antisymmetry axiom states that for all elements x and y of A, if x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ x, then x ≈₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a and c be elements of A with a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a. Instantiate the antisymmetry axiom with x = a and y = c. The two premises required are exactly a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a, which we have by assumption.
  -- Step 4: The antisymmetry axiom therefore yields a ≈₁ c, which is the required conclusion.
  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′

  -- Step 2: The same preorder structure gives reflexivity of the order up to equality: whenever x ≈₁ y, we have x ≤₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.
  -- Step 4: Case 1: a <₁ c and c <₁ e. Then a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ e, so a ≤₁ e by transitivity of ≤₁.
  -- Step 5: In Case 1, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≤₁ a by respect of ≤₁ on the right, and antisymmetry gives a ≈₁ c, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ ((Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c c≤e) , (λ z → a≉c (×-lex-trans-antisym t₁ a c a≤c (×-lex-trans-resp-right t₁ c e a (IsEquivalence.sym (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) z) c≤e)))))
  -- Step 6: Case 2: a <₁ c and c ≈₁ e, with d ≤₂ f. Since c ≈₁ e, respect of ≤₁ on the right applied to a ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 7: In Case 2, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then a ≈₁ c by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))
  -- Step 8: Case 3: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c <₁ e. Since a ≈₁ c, respect of ≤₁ on the left applied to c ≤₁ e gives a ≤₁ e.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library

-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)

  using (Pointwise)

open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

  -- dsp: lemmas

  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.
  -- Step 2: Keep only the partial order part; totality is dropped.
  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.
  ×-pw-isEquivalence t₁ t₂ = (Pointwise.×-isEquivalence (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ t₂))

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.
  -- Step 2: The antisymmetry axiom states that for all elements x and y of A, if x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ x, then x ≈₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a and c be elements of A with a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a. Instantiate the antisymmetry axiom with x = a and y = c. The two premises required are exactly a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a, which we have by assumption.
  -- Step 4: The antisymmetry axiom therefore yields a ≈₁ c, which is the required conclusion.
  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_. Its partial order component is a preorder, so the relation ≤₁ is transitive: whenever x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ z, we have x ≤₁ z.
  -- Step 2: The same preorder structure gives reflexivity of the order up to equality: whenever x ≈₁ y, we have x ≤₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.
  -- Step 4: Case 1: a <₁ c and c <₁ e. Then a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ e, so a ≤₁ e by transitivity of ≤₁.
  -- Step 5: In Case 1, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≤₁ a by respect of ≤₁ on the right, and antisymmetry gives a ≈₁ c, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ ((Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c c≤e) , (λ z → a≉c (×-lex-trans-antisym t₁ a c a≤c (×-lex-trans-resp-right t₁ c e a (IsEquivalence.sym (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) z) c≤e)))))
  -- Step 6: Case 2: a <₁ c and c ≈₁ e, with d ≤₂ f. Since c ≈₁ e, respect of ≤₁ on the right applied to a ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 7: In Case 2, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then a ≈₁ c by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))
  -- Step 8: Case 3: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c <₁ e. Since a ≈₁ c, respect of ≤₁ on the left applied to c ≤₁ e gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 9: In Case 3, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≈₁ e by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not c ≈₁ e. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≈c) c≤e , (λ z → c≉e (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) a≈c) z))))
  -- Step 10: Case 4: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c ≈₁ e with d ≤₂ f. By transitivity of ≈₁, a ≈₁ e. By transitivity of ≤₂, b ≤₂ f. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the second alternative.
  -- Step 11: The four cases exhaust all combinations of the alternatives, and in each case x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds. Hence the lexicographic order is transitive.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₂ (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) a≈c c≈e , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂)) b≤d d≤f))

  postulate
    lexantisym-gap0 : (t : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_) → (x y : A) → x ≤₁ y → y ≤₁ x → x ≈₁ y

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y x → _≋_ x y
  -- Step 2: Assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ x. Each of these hypotheses is a disjunction, so we split into four cases according to which disjunct holds for each.
  -- Case A: x₁ <₁ y₁ and y₁ <₁ x₁. Then x₁ ≤₁ y₁ and y₁ ≤₁ x₁, so antisymmetry of ≤₁ gives x₁ ≈₁ y₁. But x₁ <₁ y₁ includes x₁ ≉₁ y₁, which is a contradiction. So Case A cannot occur.

  -- Case B: x₁ <₁ y₁ and y₁ ≈₁ x₁ (with y₂ ≤₂ x₂). Symmetry of ≈₁ gives x₁ ≈₁ y₁, which contradicts x₁ ≉₁ y₁ from x₁ <₁ y₁. So Case B cannot occur.

  -- Case C: x₁ ≈₁ y₁ (with x₂ ≤₂ y₂) and y₁ <₁ x₁. Symmetry of ≈₁ gives y₁ ≈₁ x₁, which contradicts y₁ ≉₁ x₁ from y₁ <₁ x₁. So Case C cannot occur.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.

  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.

  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′

  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.
  -- Step 4: Case 1: a <₁ c and c <₁ e. Then a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ e, so a ≤₁ e by transitivity of ≤₁.
  -- Step 5: In Case 1, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≤₁ a by respect of ≤₁ on the right, and antisymmetry gives a ≈₁ c, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ ((Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c c≤e) , (λ z → a≉c (×-lex-trans-antisym t₁ a c a≤c (×-lex-trans-resp-right t₁ c e a (IsEquivalence.sym (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) z) c≤e)))))
  -- Step 6: Case 2: a <₁ c and c ≈₁ e, with d ≤₂ f. Since c ≈₁ e, respect of ≤₁ on the right applied to a ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 7: In Case 2, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then a ≈₁ c by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))
  -- Step 8: Case 3: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c <₁ e. Since a ≈₁ c, respect of ≤₁ on the left applied to c ≤₁ e gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 9: In Case 3, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≈₁ e by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not c ≈₁ e. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≈c) c≤e , (λ z → c≉e (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) a≈c) z))))
  -- Step 10: Case 4: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c ≈₁ e with d ≤₂ f. By transitivity of ≈₁, a ≈₁ e. By transitivity of ≤₂, b ≤₂ f. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the second alternative.
  -- Step 11: The four cases exhaust all combinations of the alternatives, and in each case x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds. Hence the lexicographic order is transitive.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise

open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_

    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

  -- dsp: lemmas

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z

  -- Step 6: Case 2: a <₁ c and c ≈₁ e, with d ≤₂ f. Since c ≈₁ e, respect of ≤₁ on the right applied to a ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ e.

  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.
  -- Step 3: A proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation, together with proofs that _≤₁_ is reflexive and transitive.
  -- Step 4: A proof that _≈₁_ is an equivalence relation is exactly a proof of IsEquivalence _≈₁_.
  -- Step 5: Select the partial order, preorder, and equivalence components in turn. No induction is needed, and neither totality nor antisymmetry is used.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ holds, given as a proof on the carrier with equality _≈₂_ and relation _≤₂_.
  -- Step 2: Keep only the partial order part; totality is dropped.
  -- Step 3: Keep only the preorder part; antisymmetry is dropped.
  -- Step 4: Keep the IsEquivalence _≈₂_ component of the preorder, alongside reflexivity and transitivity.
  -- Step 5: Hence IsEquivalence _≈₂_ is obtained by taking successive components of the hypothesis.
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ record { isPartialOrder = record { isPreorder = record { isEquivalence = eq } } } = eq

  ×-pw-isEquivalence : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  -- Assume both hypotheses. By the first lemma, ≈₁ and ≈₂ are equivalence relations, so only reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of ≋ remain.
  ×-pw-isEquivalence t₁ t₂ = (Pointwise.×-isEquivalence (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₂ t₂))

  ×-lex-trans-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c : A) → a ≤₁ c → c ≤₁ a → a ≈₁ c
  -- Step 1: The hypothesis is that ≤₁ is a total order with respect to ≈₁. A total order is in particular a partial order with respect to ≈₁, so the antisymmetry axiom for ≤₁ is available.
  -- Step 2: The antisymmetry axiom states that for all elements x and y of A, if x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ x, then x ≈₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a and c be elements of A with a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a. Instantiate the antisymmetry axiom with x = a and y = c. The two premises required are exactly a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ a, which we have by assumption.
  -- Step 4: The antisymmetry axiom therefore yields a ≈₁ c, which is the required conclusion.
  ×-lex-trans-antisym t a c h₁ h₂ = (IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) h₁ h₂)

  ×-lex-trans-resp-right : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c c′ : A) → c ≈₁ c′ → a ≤₁ c → a ≤₁ c′
  -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_. Its partial order component is a preorder, so the relation ≤₁ is transitive: whenever x ≤₁ y and y ≤₁ z, we have x ≤₁ z.
  -- Step 2: The same preorder structure gives reflexivity of the order up to equality: whenever x ≈₁ y, we have x ≤₁ y.
  -- Step 3: Let a, c, c′ be elements of A with c ≈₁ c′ and a ≤₁ c. By the previous step applied to the pair c ≈₁ c′, we get c ≤₁ c′.
  -- Step 4: We now have a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ c′. By the transitivity of ≤₁, it follows that a ≤₁ c′.
  ×-lex-trans-resp-right t a c c′ eq h = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) h (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t)) eq))

  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y z : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y z → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x z
  -- Step 3: Let x = (a, b), y = (c, d) and z = (e, f), and assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ z. Each hypothesis is one of two alternatives, so there are four cases.
  -- Step 4: Case 1: a <₁ c and c <₁ e. Then a ≤₁ c and c ≤₁ e, so a ≤₁ e by transitivity of ≤₁.
  -- Step 5: In Case 1, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≤₁ a by respect of ≤₁ on the right, and antisymmetry gives a ≈₁ c, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ ((Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c c≤e) , (λ z → a≉c (×-lex-trans-antisym t₁ a c a≤c (×-lex-trans-resp-right t₁ c e a (IsEquivalence.sym (isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ t₁) z) c≤e)))))
  -- Step 6: Case 2: a <₁ c and c ≈₁ e, with d ≤₂ f. Since c ≈₁ e, respect of ≤₁ on the right applied to a ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 7: In Case 2, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then a ≈₁ c by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not a ≈₁ c. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≤c (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) c≈e) , (λ z → a≉c (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) z (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) c≈e)))))
  -- Step 8: Case 3: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c <₁ e. Since a ≈₁ c, respect of ≤₁ on the left applied to c ≤₁ e gives a ≤₁ e.
  -- Step 9: In Case 3, we show not a ≈₁ e. Suppose a ≈₁ e. Then c ≈₁ e by symmetry and transitivity of ≈₁, contradicting not c ≈₁ e. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the first alternative.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₁ (c≤e , c≉e)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁)) a≈c) c≤e , (λ z → c≉e (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) a≈c) z))))
  -- Step 10: Case 4: a ≈₁ c with b ≤₂ d, and c ≈₁ e with d ≤₂ f. By transitivity of ≈₁, a ≈₁ e. By transitivity of ≤₂, b ≤₂ f. Hence x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds by the second alternative.
  -- Step 11: The four cases exhaust all combinations of the alternatives, and in each case x ≤ₗₑₓ z holds. Hence the lexicographic order is transitive.
  ×-lex-trans t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (e , f) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₂ (c≈e , d≤f)) = (inj₂ (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₁))) a≈c c≈e , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂)) b≤d d≤f))

  postulate
    lexantisym-gap0 : (t : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_) → (x y : A) → x ≤₁ y → y ≤₁ x → x ≈₁ y

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → _≤ₗₑₓ_ x y → _≤ₗₑₓ_ y x → _≋_ x y
  -- Step 2: Assume x ≤ₗₑₓ y and y ≤ₗₑₓ x. Each of these hypotheses is a disjunction, so we split into four cases according to which disjunct holds for each.
  -- Case A: x₁ <₁ y₁ and y₁ <₁ x₁. Then x₁ ≤₁ y₁ and y₁ ≤₁ x₁, so antisymmetry of ≤₁ gives x₁ ≈₁ y₁. But x₁ <₁ y₁ includes x₁ ≉₁ y₁, which is a contradiction. So Case A cannot occur.
  ×-lex-antisym t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₁ (c≤a , c≉a)) = (lexantisym-gap0 A ℓ₁ ℓ₂ B ℓ₃ ℓ₄)
  -- Case B: x₁ <₁ y₁ and y₁ ≈₁ x₁ (with y₂ ≤₂ x₂). Symmetry of ≈₁ gives x₁ ≈₁ y₁, which contradicts x₁ ≉₁ y₁ from x₁ <₁ y₁. So Case B cannot occur.
  ×-lex-antisym t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (inj₁ (a≤c , a≉c)) (inj₂ (c≈a , d≤b)) = {!!}
  -- Case C: x₁ ≈₁ y₁ (with x₂ ≤₂ y₂) and y₁ <₁ x₁. Symmetry of ≈₁ gives y₁ ≈₁ x₁, which contradicts y₁ ≉₁ x₁ from y₁ <₁ x₁. So Case C cannot occur.
  ×-lex-antisym t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₁ (c≤a , c≉a)) = {!!}
  -- Case D: x₁ ≈₁ y₁, x₂ ≤₂ y₂, and y₂ ≤₂ x₂. This is the only case that remains possible, and it gives the first component of x ≋ y directly, namely x₁ ≈₁ y₁.

  ×-lex-antisym t₁ t₂ (a , b) (c , d) (inj₂ (a≈c , b≤d)) (inj₂ (c≈a , d≤b)) = (a≈c , IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂) b≤d d≤b)

        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

  -- dsp: lemmas
  isTotalOrder-isEquivalence₁ : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₁_
  -- Step 1: A proof of IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of totality.
  -- Step 2: A proof that _≤₁_ is a partial order with respect to _≈₁_ consists of a proof that _≤₁_ is a preorder with respect to _≈₁_, together with a proof of antisymmetry.

Then a'' ≈₁ a, and since a ≤₁ a', the respect fact gives a'' ≤₁ a'. Together with a' ≤₁ a'', antisymmetry gives a' ≈₁ a'', contradicting a' not≈₁ a''. 7. [case] Case 2: x ≤lex y by the first clause and y ≤lex z by the second clause. So a ≤₁ a', a not≈₁ a', a' ≈₁ a'', and b' ≤₂ b''. Since a' ≈₁ a'', the respect fact gives a ≤₁ a''. Suppose a ≈₁ a''. Then a ≈₁ a'' and a'' ≈₁ a' give a ≈₁ a' by transitivity, contradicting a not≈₁ a'. So a not≈₁ a'', and the first clause gives x ≤lex z.
8. [case] Case 3: x ≤lex y by the second clause and y ≤lex z by the first clause. So a ≈₁ a', b ≤₂ b', a' ≤₁ a'', and a' not≈₁ a''. Since a ≈₁ a', the respect fact gives a ≤₁ a''. Suppose a ≈₁ a''. 9. [case] Case 4: x ≤lex y by the second clause and y ≤lex z by the second clause. So a ≈₁ a', b ≤₂ b', a' ≈₁ a'', and b' ≤₂ b''. By transitivity of ≈₁, a ≈₁ a''. By transitivity of ≤₂, b ≤₂ b''. So the second clause gives x ≤lex z.

17. [lemma/hard] Let x = (a,b) and y = (a',b'). Since ≈₁ is decidable, either a ≈₁ a' or a not≈₁ a'. We consider these two cases in steps 18 and 19.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  postulate
    ×-pw-refl : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → (x : A × B) → Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_ x x

  postulate
    ×-≤₁-respects : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (∀ {p q r} → p ≈₁ q → p ≤₁ r → q ≤₁ r) × (∀ {p q r} → r ≤₁ p → p ≈₁ q → r ≤₁ q)

  postulate
    ×-≤₂-respects : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (∀ {p q r} → p ≈₂ q → p ≤₂ r → q ≤₂ r) × (∀ {p q r} → r ≤₂ p → p ≈₂ q → r ≤₂ q)

  postulate
    ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_

  postulate
    ×-lex-refl : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (∀ {x y} → Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_ x y → x ≤ₗₑₓ y)

  postulate
    ×-lex-antisym : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_

  postulate
    ×-lex-total : Decidable _≈₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → Total _≤ₗₑₓ_

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-isTotalOrder : Decidable _≈₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsTotalOrder _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  postulate
    strictTransitive : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a a' a'' : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a a' → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a' a'' → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a a''

  postulate
    strictRespectsEquivL : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a b c : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≈₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c

  postulate
    strictRespectsEquivR : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a b c : A) → a ≈₁ b → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ b c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  -- Case 1: a <₁ a' and a' <₁ a''. By the lemma strictTransitive, a <₁ a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₁ p) (inj₁ q) = {!!}
  -- Case 2: a <₁ a' and a' ≈₁ a'' with b' ≤₂ b''. Since a' ≈₁ a'', a <₁ a'' by the first part of strictRespectsEquivL, applied with b = a' and c = a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₁ p) (inj₂ (q , r)) = {!!}
  -- Case 3: a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b', and a' <₁ a''. By the second part of strictRespectsEquivR, applied with b = a' and c = a'', we get a <₁ a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₂ (p , r)) (inj₁ q) = {!!}

  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₂ (p , r)) (inj₂ (q , s)) = {!!}

-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K --safe #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)

open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

  -- Case 2: a <₁ a' and a' ≈₁ a'' with b' ≤₂ b''. Since a' ≈₁ a'', a <₁ a'' by the first part of strictRespectsEquivL, applied with b = a' and c = a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-trans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_

  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₁ p) (inj₁ q) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) (proj₁ p) (proj₁ q) , λ ac → proj₂ p (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPartialOrder.antisym (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁) (proj₁ p) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) (proj₁ q) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) ac))))))
  -- Case 2: a <₁ a' and a' ≈₁ a'' with b' ≤₂ b''. Since a' ≈₁ a'', a <₁ a'' by the first part of strictRespectsEquivL, applied with b = a' and c = a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₁ p) (inj₂ (q , r)) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) (proj₁ p) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) q) , λ ac → proj₂ p (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) ac (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) q))))
  -- Case 3: a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b', and a' <₁ a''. By the second part of strictRespectsEquivR, applied with b = a' and c = a'', we get a <₁ a''. So the first disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₂ (p , r)) (inj₁ q) = (inj₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁)) p) (proj₁ q) , λ ac → proj₂ q (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) p) ac)))
  -- Case 4: a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b', and a' ≈₁ a'' with b' ≤₂ b''. By transitivity of ≈₁, a ≈₁ a''. By transitivity of ≤₂, b ≤₂ b''. So the second disjunct of x ≤_lex z holds.
  ×-lex-trans ord₁ ord₂ (inj₂ (p , r)) (inj₂ (q , s)) = (inj₂ (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₁))) p q , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder ord₂)) r s))
